name: gas_spring_oscillator
title: Gas spring: a ball oscillating on a gas column
summary: A ball of 15 g is displaced by 5 cm in a glass tube holding 1 litre of helium; the adiabatic gas column below the ball acts as a spring and the friction damps the motion. The model integrates Newton's law for the ball with the Integral function over 5 s and returns the trajectory of the ball position, of the pressure and of the gas temperature, the period of the small oscillations and the specific heat ratio of the gas.

origin.notes: Example of the EES example library (© F-Chart Software); the plain-text mirror of the same file is published under MIT by EES-Community/ees-examples (commit 5c703d0, 2026-03-01), which is the source of the licence. The EES licence stamp of the file ({$ID$ #2177: For use by students and faculty, Dépt Ingénieur Industriel, HENALLUX, Belgium klein}) identifies the licence holder, not the author of the model. The string variable G$ (the gas of the column) is undefined in the source file; it was restored as 'Helium' from the stored solution (see README).

verification.summary: Against the solution stored in the original EES file (hand-converted): 18 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001), max 5.78e-05 on c_v (EES vs CoolProp helium properties). The trajectory agrees with the integral table stored in the file to 9e-5 m and with an independent RK4 integration of the same equations to 1.2e-7 m at the end of the integration.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of ~/Nextcloud/thermo_models/EES_library/gas spring.EES (29 variables, 1 stale record dropped) and the integral table stored in the same file (502 rows); independent Runge-Kutta 4 integration of the equations of the model
verification.notes: compare_solution.py on the shipped model against the hand-converted EES stored solution: 18 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 14 (the nine states and diagnostics acc, F, Friction, L, P, T, T_abs, V, Velocity, the integration variable time, the string variable G$ and the built-in constants g#, R#, pi). The largest deviation, 5.78e-05 on c_v, comes from the properties of the helium (EES 20785.47 J/kmol-K against CoolProp 20786.31); R differs by 1.5e-05 (EES R# 8314.34 against CoolSolve R# 8314.462618 J/kmol-K) and g by 3.6e-05. The stored EES run stopped at t = 2.5725 s (its integral table is inf beyond t = 2.57 s) while the model integrates to 5 s: the variables that depend on the end of the integration were therefore compared separately, with a re-run of the model at Time_final = 2.5725 s (28 common variables, 6 differ; the largest are L 2.89e-01 and acc 1.52e-01, i.e. 0.21 mm on an excursion of 47 mm, and Time_final 4.86e-01, the value of the re-run itself). Those deviations are the integration error of EES: an independent RK4 integration (step 1e-4 s) of the same equations with the EES constants gives L = 7.4535e-4 m at t = 2.5725 s, against 7.3508e-4 m for CoolSolve and 5.2260e-4 m for the stored EES solution. Against the integral table stored in the file (rows 51, 151 and 251, t = 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 s): 4 common variables, 1 differ (rtol=0.001) at t = 0.5 s (L, 4.79e-03) and at t = 1.5 s (L, 3.75e-03), 0 differ at t = 2.5 s; the position differs by at most 0.09 mm, P by 3.0e-05 and T by 1.6e-04.
